title: In Paradise, friends turn to each other and talk.
subtitle: Remembering the road together

row.title: the journey that got them there

then: The tafsir says {reward}the believers will draw near to each other talking{/reward} and {idea}remembering their actions and conditions in this life{/idea}, the way friends talk over a meal.
now: Picture yourself one day with the friend who prayed beside you in a cold masjid, laughing about how hard it was. {reward}The people you strive with now are your future conversation.{/reward}
old: My struggles now are just something to get through.
new: The struggles I share with good friends become stories we tell in Paradise.
try: Send a message to a friend who helps you in your faith and tell them you are grateful for them.

title: We were careful with Allah, even at home.
subtitle: Fear in the middle of family life
then: Their first memory: {idea}in the midst of our families{/idea}, the tafsir says, {idea}we were afraid of our Lord and fearful of His torment.{/idea} Their awareness of Allah was not saved for special places. It lived at home.
now: Home is where you relax. It is also where you snap at your spouse, ignore your mother's call, scroll past Isha. {idea}Mindfulness at the dinner table counts.{/idea}
old: Home is where I can be careless.
new: The way I live with my family is part of my walk with Allah.
try: At home today, catch one harsh word before it comes out and say something kind instead.

title: Allah was gracious and saved us from what we feared.
subtitle: Fear that ended in safety
then: They say: {reward}Allah has been gracious to us{/reward}, and {reward}saved us from the torment of the Fire.{/reward} The tafsir says, {idea}He granted us a favor and saved us from what we feared.{/idea} They do not credit themselves.
now: You sat by the hospital bed fearing the worst, and it passed. You panicked about the bills, and somehow they were paid. {reward}Remember who saved you.{/reward} Fear placed with Allah ends in safety.
old: I got through hard times because of my own strength.
new: When I am saved from what I feared, it is Allah's favor.
try: Recall one fear that did not come true. Thank Allah for it out loud.

title: We used to call on Him, and He is Kind and Merciful.
subtitle: The dua that was answered
then: Their last words in this scene: {idea}we used to invoke Him before.{/idea} The tafsir says they called on Him {idea}with submission and humility{/idea}, and {reward}He accepted and gave them what they wished.{/reward}
now: The dua you whisper in the car before the job interview. The one you make in sujood when no one knows what you are carrying. {reward}Those duas are not lost.{/reward} One day you may say: I used to call on Him.
old: My duas feel small and maybe unheard.
new: The duas I make now are part of how I reach Paradise.
try: Make one dua today in your own words, in sujood, for something you truly want.

title: Keep reminding. You are no fortune-teller and no madman.
subtitle: Allah defends His Prophet ﷺ

key.label: What to do with false labels

then: The surah turns to the Quraysh chiefs. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to {idea}keep conveying the message{/idea}, and answers their claims: {reward}by the grace of Allah, you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman.{/reward}
now: Someone spreads a story about you at work or in the family. You want to spend a week correcting it. {idea}Keep doing the good you were doing.{/idea} Let Allah handle your name.
old: I have to clear my name before I can carry on.
new: When I am lied about, I keep doing right and trust Allah to defend me.
try: If someone has misjudged you, do one good thing today without explaining yourself.

title: They called him a poet and waited for him to die.
subtitle: Waiting for a messenger to disappear
then: Ibn Abbas reported that the Quraysh met in Dar An-Nadwah, and one said: {trap}jail him in chains, then wait{/trap}; he will die like the poets before him. They hoped time would {trap}rid them of his message.{/trap}
now: You have a reminder you are waiting out: a nagging conscience, a friend's advice, a verse that bothers you. {idea}You hope it will fade if you ignore it long enough.{/idea} Truth does not expire.
old: If I ignore an uncomfortable truth long enough, it will go away.
new: Truth does not fade with time. Waiting it out only delays my answer.
try: Bring one ignored piece of good advice back to mind today and act on part of it.

title: Then wait. I am waiting with you.
subtitle: A calm answer to people waiting for your fall
then: Allah gives the Prophet ﷺ a short, calm reply: {idea}wait, and I too will wait with you.{/idea} The tafsir adds, {reward}you will come to know to whom the good end and triumph shall be granted{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: A rival at work is waiting for you to fail. A relative says your new path will not last. {idea}You do not need to argue.{/idea} Keep going and let time tell.
old: I have to prove them wrong right now.
new: I can calmly wait, trusting Allah to show whose path ends well.
try: When someone doubts you this week, smile, say we will see, and keep going.

title: Does your mind really tell you this, or is it pride?
subtitle: Reason or rebellion
then: The Quraysh prided themselves on being sensible. Allah asks: {idea}do their minds command them to say this{/idea}, though the tafsir says {trap}they know in their hearts it is untrue?{/trap} Or are they simply {trap}a people who transgress all bounds?{/trap}
now: You give a long logical reason for skipping something you know is right. But underneath, you just do not want to. {idea}Be honest about which one is speaking: your reason, or your resistance.{/idea}
new: Sometimes my reasons are really my resistance, dressed as logic.
try: Take one excuse you use often. Ask yourself honestly: is this reason, or reluctance?

title: They said he made it up. Really, they refused to believe.
subtitle: The accusation and its root
then: They said the Prophet ﷺ {trap}forged this Quran and brought it from his own.{/trap} Allah answers with one line: {idea}rather, they do not believe.{/idea} The tafsir says {trap}their disbelief drives them to utter these statements.{/trap}
now: When you have decided you do not like someone, every rumor about them sounds believable. {idea}The verdict came first, the reasons second.{/idea} Watch for that in yourself.
old: I doubt things because the evidence is weak.
new: Sometimes I decide first and gather reasons after.
try: Think of one person you are quick to suspect. Give them one fair benefit of the doubt today.

title: If it was made up, bring something like it.
subtitle: The challenge of the Quran
then: If he wrote it himself, Allah says, {idea}let them produce a recitation like it.{/idea} The tafsir says that even if they joined with all jinn and mankind, {reward}they would never produce something like the Quran, or ten surahs, or even one.{/reward}
now: You have read thousands of posts, articles, and books this year. How many of them changed how you pray, forgive, or sleep at night? {reward}This book has been doing that for fourteen centuries.{/reward}
old: The Quran is one great book among many.
new: The Quran stands alone, and no one has matched it.
try: Read a short surah today, slowly, and notice one line that speaks to you.

title: Did you come from nothing, or did you make yourself?
subtitle: The question that opened a heart
then: Jubayr bin Mut'im came to the Prophet ﷺ after Badr, still an idolator. He heard him recite these verses in Maghrib and said, {reward}I felt my heart would fly away.{/reward} The tafsir says this was {idea}one of the reasons he later embraced Islam.{/idea}
now: You call yourself self-made: your degree, your business, your body at the gym. But you did not make your heart beat this morning. {idea}Ask the question honestly, once.{/idea}
old: I am who I am because of my own effort.
new: I did not create myself. Someone made me, and that changes everything.
try: Put your hand on your chest, feel your heartbeat for thirty seconds, and ask who keeps it going.

title: They did not make the sky. They just lack certainty.
subtitle: Knowing, but not being sure
then: The tafsir says {idea}they knew that Allah alone is the Creator{/idea}. Yet they fell into idolatry because {trap}they had no firm belief.{/trap} Knowledge without certainty did not change how they lived.
now: You know Allah provides, but you still lose sleep over money. You know He hears, but you still do not ask. {idea}The gap between knowing and being certain is where most of us live.{/idea}
old: Knowing something about Allah is the same as being sure of it.
new: Certainty is knowledge that has reached the heart and shows in my life.
try: Pick one thing you know about Allah, and act today as if you are fully certain of it.
